guides.title: Elder-Ray Bull and Bear Power
guides.concept: Bull Power is the completed high minus an EMA; Bear Power is the completed low minus that same EMA.
guides.whyUse: This source-informed study can support careful chart interpretation when inputs and timing are verified; it is not a standalone trading signal or a verified performance claim.
guides.howToUse: Use the same seeded EMA and completed bar for both values; this shows the relationship of extremes to a trend reference, not the identity of traders.
guides.procedure: Define the price/volume feed, symbol, session, timeframe, completed-bar cutoff, period, seed and missing-data rule. Use the same seeded EMA and completed bar for both values; this shows the relationship of extremes to a trend reference, not the identity of traders.
guides.limit: Seed history and trading session must be declared; positive or negative power is not a validated trading signal.
guides.limits: Seed history and trading session must be declared; positive or negative power is not a validated trading signal.
guides.invalidation: Suspend interpretation when declared inputs, warmup, publication rights or denominators are not verified. Seed history and trading session must be declared; positive or negative power is not a validated trading signal.
guides.commonError: Claiming a positive Bull Power automatically justifies a long entry.
guides.selfCheck: FICTIONAL INDEPENDENT TRANSFER: With high $22.00, low $20.50 and an already-warmed EMA13 of $21, compute +$1 and −$0.50 separately. State calculation, units, declared settings and one invalid inference.
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded subject-specific correction: Both powers subtract the same prior-history-consistent EMA from high and low. The EMA13 is provided, not calculated from one candle. Divergences cannot be verified from a single bar, and positive bull power does not establish a certain future trade. Worked evidence: FICTIONAL: Given completed high $10.50, low $9.60 and correctly initialized EMA13(close) $10.00, Bull Power = $0.50 and Bear Power = −$0.40. These are signed differences in price units, not buyer or seller volume.

guides.title: Ease of Movement (EMV)
guides.concept: EMV relates changes in a candle midpoint to volume scaled by that candle's high-low range.
guides.whyUse: This source-informed study can support careful chart interpretation when inputs and timing are verified; it is not a standalone trading signal or a verified performance claim.
guides.howToUse: Disclose the volume scale and interval, then compare midpoint displacement and bar volume on completed OHLCV evidence.
guides.procedure: Define the price/volume feed, symbol, session, timeframe, completed-bar cutoff, period, seed and missing-data rule. Disclose the volume scale and interval, then compare midpoint displacement and bar volume on completed OHLCV evidence.
guides.limit: Zero range or volume can make the value undefined; vendors use scaling and smoothing conventions.

guides.invalidation: Suspend interpretation when declared inputs, warmup, publication rights or denominators are not verified. Zero range or volume can make the value undefined; vendors use scaling and smoothing conventions.
guides.commonError: Comparing two EMV values without matching volume scales and sessions.
guides.selfCheck: FICTIONAL INDEPENDENT TRANSFER: With midpoint move −$0.50, H−L $1.00, volume 100,000 and identical scale 100,000, calculate BoxRatio 1 and EMV −0.50. State calculation, units, declared settings and one invalid inference.
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded subject-specific correction: Ease of Movement requires two valid completed bar midpoints, nonzero high-low range and positive volume with an explicit volume scaling factor. ChartSchool commonly uses its own 100-million divisor; numeric values change with scale, so do not compare settings without normalization. Optional smoothing needs completed history. Worked evidence: FICTIONAL: Previous completed midpoint $10, current midpoint $11, current H−L range $2, volume 200,000 shares and declared volume scale 100,000 give BoxRatio = (200,000/100,000)/2 = 1 and one-period EMV = (11−10)/1 = +1 price-distance-squared per scaled-volume unit.

guides.title: Choppiness Index
guides.concept: Choppiness compares cumulative true range with the same window's highest high to lowest low.
guides.whyUse: This source-informed study can support careful chart interpretation when inputs and timing are verified; it is not a standalone trading signal or a verified performance claim.
guides.howToUse: Interpret a completed range and accumulated travel separately; do not infer that low choppiness predicts a breakout.
guides.procedure: Define the price/volume feed, symbol, session, timeframe, completed-bar cutoff, period, seed and missing-data rule. Interpret a completed range and accumulated travel separately; do not infer that low choppiness predicts a breakout.
guides.limit: Zero high-low span or insufficient history makes the ratio undefined.

guides.invalidation: Suspend interpretation when declared inputs, warmup, publication rights or denominators are not verified. Zero high-low span or insufficient history makes the ratio undefined.
guides.commonError: Calling a low CHOP reading guaranteed trend continuation.
guides.selfCheck: FICTIONAL INDEPENDENT TRANSFER: If n=4, sum TR=$8 and HH−LL=$4, calculate 50 again; explain why zero range or n=1 makes the formula invalid. State calculation, units, declared settings and one invalid inference.
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded subject-specific correction: CHOP is a normalized summary of accumulated range relative to the full period's high-low span, not a measure of price direction. The 4-bar illustration is pedagogical; platform defaults can be longer. Require n>1, sum TR>0 and HH−LL>0, and use gap-aware true ranges. Worked evidence: FICTIONAL: Over n=4 completed bars, sum of true ranges is $12 and highest-high minus lowest-low is $6. CHOP = 100×log10(12/6)/log10(4)=50.0 index points, with valid prior closes and complete bars.

guides.title: Vortex Indicator
guides.concept: Positive and negative vortex movement compare the current high/low against the opposite prior-bar extreme.
guides.whyUse: This source-informed study can support careful chart interpretation when inputs and timing are verified; it is not a standalone trading signal or a verified performance claim.
guides.howToUse: Compute both movement sums and the true-range sum from completed OHLC data before considering a crossover.

guides.limit: Requires a preceding bar and nonzero true-range denominator; crosses may reverse.

guides.invalidation: Suspend interpretation when declared inputs, warmup, publication rights or denominators are not verified. Requires a preceding bar and nonzero true-range denominator; crosses may reverse.
guides.commonError: Treating a crossover as certain reversal evidence.
guides.selfCheck: FICTIONAL INDEPENDENT TRANSFER: If summed VM+ is 12, summed VM− is 8 and summed TR is 10 for the same window, calculate VI+=1.2 and VI−=0.8. State calculation, units, declared settings and one invalid inference.
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded subject-specific correction: Vortex values require correctly aligned prior-bar highs and lows and the same complete n-bar range for movement and true range. Values above one can occur; do not clamp these ratios as percentages. A missing prior bar or zero summed TR prevents a defensible value. Worked evidence: FICTIONAL: One completed bar has high $12 and low $10; prior bar had high $11 and low $9. VM+ = |12−9|=$3; VM−=|10−11|=$1; with valid declared period sum TR=$4, one-period VI+=0.75 and VI−=0.25.

guides.title: Ultimate Oscillator
guides.concept: The Ultimate Oscillator combines buying-pressure fractions across overlapping 7, 14 and 28 bar windows.
guides.whyUse: This source-informed study can support careful chart interpretation when inputs and timing are verified; it is not a standalone trading signal or a verified performance claim.
guides.howToUse: Show each sum before weighting, and explain that short-window evidence receives greater weight.
guides.procedure: Define the price/volume feed, symbol, session, timeframe, completed-bar cutoff, period, seed and missing-data rule. Show each sum before weighting, and explain that short-window evidence receives greater weight.
guides.limit: Needs prior closes, completed windows and positive TR sums; divergence is not a reliable forecast.
guides.limits: Needs prior closes, completed windows and positive TR sums; divergence is not a reliable forecast.
guides.invalidation: Suspend interpretation when declared inputs, warmup, publication rights or denominators are not verified. Needs prior closes, completed windows and positive TR sums; divergence is not a reliable forecast.
guides.commonError: Calling three overlapping windows three independent observations.
guides.selfCheck: FICTIONAL INDEPENDENT TRANSFER: With ratios 0.50,0.50,0.50 compute 50.0 and state why any zero TR sum makes that ratio unavailable. State calculation, units, declared settings and one invalid inference.
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded subject-specific correction: The default three windows are 7/14/28 with 4:2:1 weights. Buying pressure is close minus min(low, previous close), and true range is max(high, previous close) minus min(low, previous close). Only confirmed completed bars count. The oscillator alone does not prove a future reversal. Worked evidence: FICTIONAL: Declare already-computed completed-window ratios BP7/TR7=0.60, BP14/TR14=0.50 and BP28/TR28=0.40. Ultimate Oscillator = 100×(4×0.60+2×0.50+0.40)/7≈54.2857 points; no 28-bar history is being reconstructed.

guides.title: True Strength Index
guides.concept: TSI relates doubly smoothed price changes to doubly smoothed absolute price changes.
guides.whyUse: This source-informed study can support careful chart interpretation when inputs and timing are verified; it is not a standalone trading signal or a verified performance claim.
guides.howToUse: Compute price momentum and absolute momentum separately; then compare their smoothed ratio.

guides.limit: EMA warmup and seed convention affect the result; denominator can be zero.

guides.invalidation: Suspend interpretation when declared inputs, warmup, publication rights or denominators are not verified. EMA warmup and seed convention affect the result; denominator can be zero.
guides.commonError: Assuming doubled smoothing creates a precise next-price forecast.
guides.selfCheck: FICTIONAL INDEPENDENT TRANSFER: Given signed double EMA −0.15 and absolute double EMA +0.30, calculate −50; identify the denominator-zero case. State calculation, units, declared settings and one invalid inference.
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded subject-specific correction: TSI applies the same chained smoothing rule to price change and absolute price change; the smoothings require adequate prior bars and declared seeding. Worked evidence: FICTIONAL: Given correctly warmed double-smoothed signed close change +$0.20 and double-smoothed absolute close change $0.50 for matching 25/13 EMA settings, TSI=100×0.20/0.50=+40 points. guides.title: Ulcer Index
guides.concept: Ulcer Index measures the size and persistence of close-to-peak drawdowns over a declared window.
guides.whyUse: This source-informed study can support careful chart interpretation when inputs and timing are verified; it is not a standalone trading signal or a verified performance claim.
guides.howToUse: Compute each nonpositive percentage drawdown using a documented rolling maximum before averaging squares.
guides.procedure: Define the price/volume feed, symbol, session, timeframe, completed-bar cutoff, period, seed and missing-data rule. Compute each nonpositive percentage drawdown using a documented rolling maximum before averaging squares.
guides.limit: Changing window or adjusted close source changes the result; not a probability forecast.

guides.invalidation: Suspend interpretation when declared inputs, warmup, publication rights or denominators are not verified. Changing window or adjusted close source changes the result; not a probability forecast.
guides.commonError: Interpreting Ulcer Index as a symmetric volatility measure or a guaranteed loss.
guides.selfCheck: FICTIONAL INDEPENDENT TRANSFER: For drawdowns −6%, −3%, 0%, compute sqrt((36+9)/3)≈3.873 percentage points. State calculation, units, declared settings and one invalid inference.
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded subject-specific correction: Ulcer Index uses negative percentage drawdown relative to the qualifying running or rolling maximum and the root mean square across the declared window. Worked evidence: FICTIONAL: Three fully defined prior-peak-relative drawdowns are −10%, −5% and 0%. UI=sqrt((100+25+0)/3)≈6.455 percentage points. guides.title: Mass Index
guides.concept: Mass Index accumulates ratios of one EMA of completed high-low ranges to a second EMA of that EMA.
guides.whyUse: This source-informed study can support careful chart interpretation when inputs and timing are verified; it is not a standalone trading signal or a verified performance claim.

guides.commonError: Using a large Mass Index as a specific buy-or-sell trigger.
guides.selfCheck: FICTIONAL INDEPENDENT TRANSFER: If three consecutive fully warmed EMA(range)/EMA(EMA(range)) ratios equal 1.0, 1.2, 0.9, what is their 3-term sum and why is it not the 25-period index? State calculation, units, declared settings and one invalid inference.
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded subject-specific correction: Mass Index accumulates ratios of 9-period EMA of daily ranges to a second 9-period EMA of the same first EMA; the conventional summation uses 25 periods. Do not invent those EMAs or use the two-term demonstration as a published 25-period value. Range expansion by itself does not establish the direction of a breakout. Worked evidence: FICTIONAL: For a two-period toy sum, prewarmed single/double EMA high-low range ratios 1.10 and 1.20 yield a mass-index-style sum 2.30. guides.title: Negative Volume Index
guides.concept: NVI is a seeded cumulative price index updated only when volume decreases relative to the preceding completed bar.
guides.formula: If V(t)<V(t-1), NVI(t)=NVI(t-1)*Close(t)/Close(t-1); otherwise retain NVI.
guides.whyUse: This source-informed study can support careful chart interpretation when inputs and timing are verified; it is not a standalone trading signal or a verified performance claim.
guides.howToUse: Declare an arbitrary positive seed and which bars satisfy strictly lower volume.
guides.procedure: Define the price/volume feed, symbol, session, timeframe, completed-bar cutoff, period, seed and missing-data rule. Declare an arbitrary positive seed and which bars satisfy strictly lower volume.
guides.limit: Requires nonzero prior close; neither lower volume nor the index identifies institutional traders.
guides.limits: Requires nonzero prior close; neither lower volume nor the index identifies institutional traders.
guides.invalidation: Suspend interpretation when declared inputs, warmup, publication rights or denominators are not verified. Requires nonzero prior close; neither lower volume nor the index identifies institutional traders.
guides.commonError: Equating shrinking share volume with informed accumulation.
guides.selfCheck: FICTIONAL INDEPENDENT TRANSFER: With prior NVI=1,000, close $20 then $18, and lower volume on the second bar, compute NVI=900; describe what happens on equal volume. State calculation, units, declared settings and one invalid inference.
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded subject-specific correction: The Fosback price-relative version updates only on lower-volume completed bars, using consistent adjusted closes and a strictly positive prior close. NVI seed values and long signal EMA settings are conventions; the old breadth-based original variant differs, so do not claim a unique universal historical value. Worked evidence: FICTIONAL: Starting a declared NVI at 1,000, previous completed close $10 and current close $11, while current volume 800 is below prior volume 1,000, produces NVI=1000×(11/10)=1100 index points. Without a volume decrease, NVI would remain 1000.

guides.title: Detrended Price Oscillator
guides.concept: DPO subtracts a moving-average reference from a deliberately displaced historical price to reduce trend effects.
guides.formula: DPO at current calculation time=Close(t-shift)-SMA_N(t), shift=floor(N/2)+1; display alignment varies by platform.
guides.whyUse: This source-informed study can support careful chart interpretation when inputs and timing are verified; it is not a standalone trading signal or a verified performance claim.
guides.howToUse: Explain the historical offset, the data available at computation time, and the plotted timestamp separately.
guides.procedure: Define the price/volume feed, symbol, session, timeframe, completed-bar cutoff, period, seed and missing-data rule. Explain the historical offset, the data available at computation time, and the plotted timestamp separately.
guides.limit: A centered displayed DPO can be hindsight-dependent and may not be available at the apparent past decision point.
guides.limits: A centered displayed DPO can be hindsight-dependent and may not be available at the apparent past decision point.
guides.invalidation: Suspend interpretation when declared inputs, warmup, publication rights or denominators are not verified. A centered displayed DPO can be hindsight-dependent and may not be available at the apparent past decision point.
guides.commonError: Reading a centered hindsight DPO as a real-time predictive signal.
guides.selfCheck: FICTIONAL INDEPENDENT TRANSFER: With DPO period 20, displaced close at t−11=$46 and fully known SMA20 at t=$48, calculate −$2 and state which bar can use that information. State calculation, units, declared settings and one invalid inference.
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded subject-specific correction: StockCharts defines DPO(n) using price floor(n/2)+1 periods ago minus the n-period SMA calculated at the current time, plotted at its historical displacement. The plotted past point uses later bars: do not expose it at its old timestamp in replay before the underlying SMA is complete. DPO is for cycle study, not a present-bar trigger. Worked evidence: FICTIONAL: At calculation time t, a completed 20-period SMA is $50 and the completed close from t−11 is $52. DPO20=$52−$50=+$2. The value belongs to a displaced historical plot position, not the price visible at time t as a live momentum reading.

guides.title: Fisher Transform
guides.concept: A Fisher Transform maps a bounded normalized price-derived input through a nonlinear logarithmic transform.
guides.formula: Fisher(x)=0.5*ln((1+x)/(1-x)); normalization and clamp must be specified for -1<x<1.
guides.whyUse: This source-informed study can support careful chart interpretation when inputs and timing are verified; it is not a standalone trading signal or a verified performance claim.
guides.howToUse: Demonstrate first how completed-bar price is normalized and clipped, then interpret the transform only as transformed data.

guides.limit: Without normalization details and strict clipping the formula is undefined near the boundaries.

guides.invalidation: Suspend interpretation when declared inputs, warmup, publication rights or denominators are not verified. Without normalization details and strict clipping the formula is undefined near the boundaries.
guides.commonError: Calling large transformed readings proof of a future reversal.
guides.selfCheck: FICTIONAL INDEPENDENT TRANSFER: Compute Fisher(0.25)≈0.255413 and name why x=1 would be undefined without an explicit clamp. State calculation, units, declared settings and one invalid inference.
guides.reviewExplanation: Ungraded subject-specific correction: The Fisher transform maps a strictly inside-(−1,+1) normalized input to an unbounded transformed value. A full platform study may smooth, recursively normalize high-low median prices and clamp near endpoints; copying the transform alone does not recreate a complete vendor indicator. It does not prove the next market turn. Worked evidence: FICTIONAL: For a declared, pre-normalized bounded x=0.5, Fisher(x)=0.5×ln((1+0.5)/(1−0.5))≈+0.549306. With x=−0.5, the result is −0.549306, and x=0 yields zero; the underlying price-normalization scheme is not inferred.
